scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh booted papercusp-desktop on its own Xvfb display and drove the launcher Identity combobox in the real webview (2026-09-30T03:27:54.381Z -> 2026-09-30T03:28:08.459Z). The default input reads 'SU' and SU is the first option. The catalog loaded in 3 pages and rendered 25 of 25 expected options, with none missing or extra. Invalid and ineligible identities stay visible with a reason (true/true), and no disabled option lacks one. The first attempt exited 1 in its prepare phase: rsync exit 24 on a peer's temporary file that vanished during the operator source snapshot (docs/evidence/p2p-coordination-r1-origin-visible-delivery-2026-09-30.json.tmp.3329331.190f6bbac844) was treated as fatal. scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh now tolerates rsync exit 24 only, covered by apps/operator/lib/verify-tauri-headless-source-snapshot.test.ts. The retry passed.

The subject's activation rows were joined to the CTRL hook-context lines in its own native transcripts (470e6345, b1bced5e, 788e9549, ff4bcf63). For generations 3, 5, 8, prepared < native emission < applied, and the applied row names the native that received the emission. Generations 7 and 11 are relaunch paths (warm respawn, --resume): the new native started on the re-rendered spec, its applied row is the acknowledgment, and the CTRL line follows it. Generation 2 was emitted at launch (line 8 of 470e6345 (full-resync)), then superseded by generation 3 before an acknowledgment turn: it has a prepared row and no applied row. Generations 9, 12 changed control state only (loop/carry), emitted CTRL and wrote no activation rows. No generation reports applied without a prior emission, and no ordering violation exists.

The refreshed render is proven by the file hash and by the next native (ff4bcf63).

Generations 4 and 6 (couple/decouple) have no CTRL hook-context line and no activation rows; the subject read them through coord:orient.

Cold forks receive their carry through loop-fire COLD LOOP WAKE prompts. 788e9549's second systemPrompt part (a carry document) is inherited from its warm-respawned parent; ff4bcf63, forked from the resumed process, has one part.

The first resume attempt forked (its source host was still alive) and minted a separate identity; that fork is excluded, and the same-owner resume was re-run after stopping the host.
